page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is a general-purpose, Arm-based virtual machine instance powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The configuration provides 8 dedicated physical CPU cores without multithreading (1 thread per core), accompanied by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across multi-threaded operations and data serving tasks, enabled by dedicated single-threaded physical cores. The instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 6000.0 and delivers 10.91 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. Static web serving throughput reaches 10.09 GB/sec, alongside multi-threaded Clang compilation scoring 9005.0. However, single-core processing shows distinct limits, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1073.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the lower quartile. Similarly, the absence of vector extensions such as AVX limits small-model LLM text generation to 32.29 tokens per second.

In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, the Ampere architecture provides resource-efficient multi-tenant density with dedicated compute cores that avoid hyperthreading contention. Because there is no bundled local storage or included public IPv4 addresses, storage and routing overhead must be budgeted separately. The t2a-standard-8 is best suited for horizontally scaled web servers, API endpoints, microservices architectures, Redis in-memory caches, and multi-threaded development compilation pipelines running on ARM-native environments.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring an 8-core Ampere Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, coupled with 32.0 GB of system memory. Operating on dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core and no hyperthreading, the instance provides steady execution across concurrent tasks, registering 10.91 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 10.09 GB/sec in static web throughput. The configuration bundles no local storage and zero GPUs, relying instead on network-attached persistence. While single-thread performance is modest, as reflected in lower single-core Geekbench and compression metrics, the consistent multi-core execution profile makes the instance cost-efficient for web serving, microservices, containerized services, caching layers, and ARM64-targeted software build pipelines.
